name: Abernys: Bogwater
notes: Built from Praxis — Bogwater Module Plan and the Abernys docs (Fenmire, the Woed, Cairn Maw, Port Covenant). Owner material: Fenmire, Bogwater, the Council of Crones, the bog-keeper, witchcraft, the Woed, tamecap and Rabitis, and the roles of Nest, Morwen, Cadfan and Meurig (spelled Meyrick here, a proposal). Everything marked canonStatus "draft" is a suggestion for the owner. Day 1 is day 243 of the default calendar, Friday 1 September. Rooms are child places with free hops, standing in for partitions until Praxis has them. Thread outcomes are states: the-spark (world), ink-claim and ink-mark (the runaway), rabitis (Lowri), and schedules wait on them.

identity.name: Abernys
identity.description: An island of layered migrations: first peoples with no memory of arriving, later waves that migrated, conquered and mixed, and humans as the latest.
identity.tone: grim, wet and dangerous, with room for hijinks

importantFacts: The first peoples are prey peoples, and both conquests that followed were by predators. Humans are neither, so nobody on Abernys knows how to read them.

Port Covenant indentures the poor by contract, and inks its punitive indentures into the skin, where anyone who reads the Arbiters' hand can read them. Its patrols hunt runaways and clash with the fen.
The fen folk answer to the Council of Crones at Bogwater, and the bog-keeper speaks for them to outsiders. They kill trespassers on their family islands, burn their dead, and let no slaver leave.
Fen witchcraft is ritual and alchemical. Both the craft and the witches are distrusted, even by the fen folk who buy from them.
The Woed is a living wood joined to the Whispering Woods. It stays ordinary until it notices someone, and it notices the lost and the hopeless. The Hushed live with it and sell what it gives.
Rabitis turns the afflicted feral. Tamecap, a mushroom found only in the Woed, cures it in its early stages, and nothing else is known to.

rules.constraints: Fen witchcraft is ritual and alchemical; nothing about it is confirmed supernatural. The Woed's menace is selective, intimate and psychological, never a jump scare or a curse on everyone. How Rabitis spreads, and anything about it beyond its effects and its cure, stays unknown.

timeWeather.note: Draft season lines for Fenmire. Not yet read by the engine.

seasons.autumn: Fog most mornings, the eel run on dark nights, smoke over Bogwater.
seasons.winter: Floods, ice at the edges, reed cutting; families keep to their islands.
seasons.summer: Midges, fever, salt boiled on the coast.

places.name: Abernys
places.description: An island of layered migrations a month or two's sail from Bitterroot: first peoples with no memory of arriving, later waves that conquered and mixed, and humans as the latest.

places.name: Fenmire
places.description: The hard, wet country between the Woed and the south coast: reed beds, meres, peat bog and islands of firm ground where families build. A backwater even in the first peoples' own eyes, and proud of it.

places.name: Bogwater
places.description: The fen's trading post, on the biggest island near open water: a dock, an alehouse, the Crones' round hall and a few dozen houses on stilts, joined by plank walks that sink a finger's width under every step. Outsiders may trade here, under suspicion; the family islands beyond are closed to them.

places.name: The landing
places.description: Bogwater's dock and smokehouse, where the fen sells to the outside, and as far in as most outsiders get. Eel barrels stand three high under reed thatch, and peat smoke from the smokehouse lies flat over the water.

places.name: The dock
places.description: Plank piers on tarred posts and mooring rings, where the Caerwyn boat ties up on Mondays and the flatboats wait for fares.

places.name: The smokehouse
places.description: A low black shed where eels hang on rods over peat fires, worked day and night in the eel run. The smoke gets into everything and everyone in it.

places.name: Cadfan's store
places.description: Shelves of rope, salt, iron hooks and stoppered jars of Morwen's remedies, the barrels Cadfan packs himself, and his bed behind a curtain at the back.

places.name: The Myrtle
places.description: Bogwater's alehouse, named for the bog myrtle in its ale, and the only place in the fen that will sell an outsider a bed. A long room under sagging thatch, benches black with use, a peat fire in a pit in the floor.

places.name: The taproom
places.description: The benches, the fire pit and Bronwen's barrels, and whoever is drinking.

places.name: The loft
places.description: Straw pallets under the thatch, up a ladder through a trap door that Bronwen bolts from below at closing.

places.name: The Crones' house
places.description: A round hall of tarred alder posts and reed walls, the biggest building in Bogwater, where the Council of Crones sits around a fire nobody lets go out.

places.name: The hall
places.description: The ring of seats around the fire. Swept and empty except on sitting day, when every Crone in the fen is in it.

places.name: Meyrick's room
places.description: A side room with a cot, a table and a stool for whoever has come to bargain with the bog-keeper.

places.name: The burning ground
places.description: A scorched stone floor outside the hall, facing open water, with dry peat and driftwood stacked under a lean-to. The fen burns its dead here, so no soul is trapped.

places.name: Nest's island
places.description: A salamander family's island of firm ground, ringed with sharpened stakes: a longhouse, smoking racks, and flatboats tied up three deep. Nobody lands uninvited, and killing a trespasser here is no crime.

places.name: The jetty
places.description: The one way in, a plank jetty outside the stakes, where visitors stop and shout.

places.name: The longhouse
places.description: Three generations of Nest's family under one roof, the hearth in the middle, and Nest's chair nearest it.

places.name: Morwen's island
places.description: A small island well out from the others: one hut, racks of moss and willow bark drying, and a door with a hatch in it at shoulder height.

places.name: Morwen's door
places.description: Where people come for remedies. Morwen talks through the hatch and sells over the sill.

places.name: The workroom
places.description: Pots, a fire, jars on every shelf, and a chest with an iron hasp. A second door at the back is barred from this side.

places.name: The back room
places.description: Behind the barred door: a pallet, a bucket, and claw marks on the inside of the door.

places.name: The eel traps
places.description: Wicker fences staked across the channel where it narrows, steering eels into nets and traps, with plank walks along the top. On run nights the crews work them by lantern.

places.name: The long fence
places.description: Nest's family's fence, the longest and nearest Bogwater.

places.name: The bend fence
places.description: The fence at the channel's bend, claimed by Nest's family and Tegan's both, and worked by whoever gets there first.

places.name: The channel
places.description: Open water below the fences, the way down to the Afon and Caerwyn, where the patrol has started stopping boats.

places.name: The fen
places.description: The open fen around Bogwater: reed beds taller than a standing hare, cut by narrow water, old peat diggings flooded into black pools, and wide shallow water where the ducks sit. Fog closes the ways to anyone who hasn't learned them.

places.name: The reed beds
places.description: Reeds over your head on every side and water underfoot. People hide here, get lost here, and get hunted here.

places.name: The peat diggings
places.description: Plank paths between flooded cuts, where peat is dug and stacked to dry by day.

places.name: The open water
places.description: Shallow water to the knee and wide to the horizon, with wildfowlers' hides of woven reed along the edges.

places.name: Grey Water
places.description: A wide grey lake at the fen's edge, where the old causeway to Nospier Point runs out across the water on rotten posts. The patrol camps on the dry end when its rota brings it.

places.name: The Woed's edge
places.description: Where the reeds give way to alders standing in black water and the Woed begins. Gatherers meet buyers on a strip of firm ground before the trees; past it the Hushed's plank bridges go in, and nobody goes in alone.

places.name: The far islands
places.description: The family islands deep in the fen, beyond Bogwater, where most of the Crones live. Outsiders don't go there.

places.name: The Woed
places.description: A boggy forest along the Afon's middle reaches, joined to the Whispering Woods through roots too deep to trace. It stays an ordinary wood until it notices someone.

places.name: The Fold
places.description: The Hushed's settlement, deep in the Woed and reached only by their plank bridges.

places.name: Port Covenant
places.description: The human colony on Nospier Point, where nothing binds anyone until they sign and no one enters without signing.

places.name: Caerwyn
places.description: The coastal city-state at the mouth of the Afon, where the fen sells its eels, peat and remedies.

places.name: Cairn Maw
places.description: Chalk uplands inland, held by three first-peoples clans who share a grievance and not a government.

places.name: The Aurochs downs
places.description: Clan Aurochs's chalk downs, running south toward Port Covenant.

species.name: Humans
species.description: The latest arrivals: colonizers at Port Covenant, thralls on the wreck coast, mudflat dwellers in Caerwyn. Neither predator nor prey, so nobody on Abernys knows how to read them.

species.name: Harefolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic rabbits and hares. On Abernys, first peoples, among them the hare families of Fenmire.

species.name: Badgerfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic badger peoples. On Abernys, first peoples, among them the badger families of Fenmire.

species.name: Salamanders
species.description: Anthropomorphic salamander peoples of Abernys, first peoples who stayed in the fens. Salamander communities are often built around water, night work and long family memory, with slow, low music made for wet nights and gatherings across the water.
species.physicalNotes: Smooth, damp skin with no fur or scales, which cracks if it dries out; long tails; dark skin with bold blotches of yellow, orange or red that fade with age. Slow and stiff in the cold, quick in the wet, and at home in the dark. A lost toe or tail tip grows back over a season, never quite straight.

socialCharacter: slow to trust and slower to forgive
keep their word and their grudges
culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Slow call-and-answer songs carried across water at night, over drums, drones and the rhythm of poling a boat.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: A rolling pulse that matches poling a boat, long held notes, and sudden silences.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Call-and-answer between boats, a low drone under a single voice, and long family songs that name who wronged whom.

species.name: Jackalopes
species.description: Rare hare and cervid hybrids, with hare's ears and antlers.

species.name: Bovinefolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Aurochs of Cairn Maw, the biggest people on the downs.

species.name: Foxfolk
species.description: Earlier migration from Bitterroot, by a route nobody remembers; many of Caerwyn's merchant houses.

factions.name: The Arbiters
factions.description: Port Covenant's monastic order of notaries, who make and keep the Pact's contracts.

factions.name: The garrison
factions.description: Port Covenant's soldiers. Its patrols survey land, hunt runaways and guard diggers, and clash with the fen.

factions.name: The Low Road
factions.description: Smugglers who get escaped thralls and runaways to Caerwyn, charge what they can pay, and sometimes sell them on.

societies.name: The fen folk
societies.description: Harefolk, badgerfolk and salamanders who stayed in the fens: proud, independent and distrustful of outsiders. The Council of Crones, the oldest family matriarchs, settles every matter at Bogwater, and the bog-keeper speaks for the fen to others.
societies.customs: Families live in private, defensive clusters, and killing a trespasser is no crime. The dead are burned, never buried, so no soul can be trapped. Owning people is forbidden, and slavers caught in the fen don't leave.

societies.name: The Hushed
societies.description: A communal cult that lives with the Woed under the Paterfamilias. Nobody goes anywhere alone, and members trade and guide but don't socialize with outsiders. The fen won't deal with them.

societies.name: The Pact
societies.description: Port Covenant's colonists. Nothing binds anyone until they sign; most of the poor are indentured; the most important contracts are tattooed on the body.

societies.name: Clan Aurochs
societies.description: Cattle folk of Cairn Maw, slow to start anything and hard to stop. Their head, Brond, wants war on Port Covenant, and needs the other clans and the fen to make it.

families.name: Nest's family
families.description: A salamander family on its own island near Bogwater, which works the long fence. Its head sits on the Council.

memories.title: Owen's death at Grey Water
memories.description: A colony patrol killed Owen, Nest's son and Ellis's father, at Grey Water. The fen burned him, and Nest kept the family from answering it.

memories.title: The baby at Bogwater's edge
memories.description: Someone left a baby girl at the edge of Bogwater. Morwen took her in, and nobody asked whose she was.

memories.title: The drowned passenger
memories.description: A Low Road passenger drowned when the patrol stopped Cadfan's boat on the channel. Cadfan pulled the body out and kept it under the barrels in the smokehouse, waiting for a burning nobody will allow an outsider.

memories.title: The bend fence quarrel
memories.description: Nest's family and Tegan's both claim the bend fence, and it comes before the Crones every autumn.

characters.name: The runaway
characters.description: A human who walked off a shipwright's indenture in Port Covenant two days ago, with the Pact's contract inked down the inside of the left forearm.
characters.appearance: Wet to the waist, two days of mud, and the Pact's black lines from wrist to elbow.
characters.draftNote: The default test character. The player can change any of it.

characters.name: Nest
characters.description: The eldest of the Council of Crones, who speaks last at every sitting and remembers which family wronged which three generations back.
characters.appearance: Her skin has gone dull and dry with age, the yellow spots faded nearly to grey, and she walks with a boat pole she uses as a staff.
characters.personality: Lets everyone else speak first, then rules. Never raises her voice; lowers it, so the room has to lean in. Keeps every grudge in order and trades one away when the price is right.
characters.speech: Slow and quiet. Answers a question with a family's name and a year.

rows.doing: in her chair by the hearth, hearing who wants what
in her chair by the hearth

characters.draftNote: Role and appearance are owner material (Fenmire doc); everything else is draft.

characters.name: Ellis
characters.description: Nest's grandson, who runs his family's crew at the long fence and wants the colony patrol dead.
characters.appearance: Lean and glossy black, orange blotches down his back, and an eel spear he carries everywhere, its barbs wrapped in rag indoors.
characters.personality: Laughs first and loudest. Picks fights with anyone older and drops them the moment Nest says his name. Counts the patrol's men out loud every time he sees them.
characters.speech: Fast, and too loud for the room. Talks about the patrol in the past tense.

characters.appearance: Two young salamanders, black with yellow blotches, mud to the elbows.
characters.personality: Laugh when Ellis laughs. Fight when Ellis fights.

characters.name: Morwen
characters.description: The fen's witch, who sells remedies through a hatch in her door and lives alone on her own island with a girl someone left at Bogwater's edge.
characters.appearance: Lean and dun, fingers stained brown to the second knuckle, and she smells of peat smoke and bog myrtle.
characters.personality: Sells first and asks nothing. These days she bars her door by noon and answers it with a knife in her other hand.
characters.speech: Doses and prices, in that order. A question gets the price again.

characters.name: Lowri
characters.description: Morwen's ward, a girl of eleven left at Bogwater's edge as a baby and raised in the witch's craft.
characters.appearance: Small and sandy, a white blaze down her face, fingers already stained from Morwen's pots.
characters.personality: Quick, curious and fond of mud. Lately she doesn't answer to her name, and sleeps through the day.
characters.speech: Used to talk through every chore. Now she hums one note, over and over.

rows.doing: asleep by the fire, thin and pale

characters.name: Cadfan
characters.description: A fen trader who runs the store and smokehouse at Bogwater's landing, and takes the fen's barrels down the channel to Caerwyn every week.
characters.appearance: Broad and heavy-shouldered, the white of his face stripe gone yellow at the edges.
characters.personality: Easier with outsiders than fen folk ought to be, and the islands don't trust him for it. Counts the barrels twice and the coin once. Gets runaways downriver for a price, and doesn't say what happens at the other end.
characters.speech: Friendly and round, all cousin and friend, and never a straight number.

characters.name: Tegan
characters.description: A Crone of the Council and Cadfan's mother, head of a badger family on the far islands that has fought Nest's family over the bend fence for three generations.
characters.appearance: Heavy and grizzled, her face stripes nearly gone, with a necklace of fish hooks that clinks when she walks.
characters.personality: Blunt and loud in a hall that prizes quiet. Votes against Nest on principle and against outsiders on instinct. Asks after Cadfan's health in the same breath as his prices.
characters.speech: Loud, short, and full of fish-market insults.

rows.doing: at home on the far islands
telling everyone what Nest got wrong

characters.name: Meyrick
characters.description: The bog-keeper, the man the Crones chose to speak for the fen to outsiders, and the only fen voice the colony will listen to.
characters.appearance: Big and grey-brown, with long hare's ears and a jackalope's antlers, one tine snapped off.
characters.personality: Says little and promises less, which suits the Crones. Outsiders find him reasonable; at home that counts against him. Stands while others sit, until Nest tells him otherwise.
characters.speech: Slow, and never a promise. Repeats your offer back to you so you hear how it sounds.

rows.doing: watching the boats and the outsiders on them
writing up the day for the Crones

characters.draftNote: The Fenmire doc names him Meurig; Meyrick is the proposed spelling. Role, ears and the snapped tine are owner material.

characters.name: Bronwen
characters.description: Keeps the Myrtle, Bogwater's alehouse and the only place in the fen an outsider can buy a bed.
characters.appearance: A brown hare with one ear notched to the root, sleeves pinned past the elbow, and a ring of keys on a cord that she thumbs while anyone pays.
characters.personality: Takes coin first and never asks names. Waters the ale for colony accents. Throws out fighters herself, with the poker she keeps in the fire pit.
characters.speech: Prices, mostly. Answers a question with what it costs.

rows.doing: asleep behind the bar, the loft bolted

characters.name: Gethin
characters.description: Bronwen's son, who poles a flatboat for fares from Bogwater's dock and takes anyone anywhere if they pay first.
characters.appearance: A long-legged brown hare with brass rings in both ears and a boat pole he never puts down.
characters.personality: Cheerful, cheap and loose-mouthed after two drinks. Takes the fare first, then asks where.
characters.speech: Talks over his shoulder while he poles, mostly about other people's business.

rows.doing: waiting for fares with his flatboat

characters.name: Edric
characters.description: A great house's eel buyer from Caerwyn, who comes on the boat every Monday and pays the fen less than last year.
characters.appearance: Rust-red with black legs, a Caerwyn coat with horn buttons, and a strongbox chained to his left wrist.
characters.personality: Pleasant, punctual and never in a hurry to pay. Remembers every trader's debts and none of their names.
characters.speech: City-smooth, full of regret about prices he set himself.

characters.name: Corran
characters.description: Clan Aurochs's envoy to the fen, lodging at the Myrtle while he asks who would fight if the host gathered.
characters.appearance: Black-hided and bigger than anyone in Bogwater, a pale stripe down his spine, horns tipped sideways to clear the Myrtle's door. Chalk dust ground into the hair of his forearms.
characters.personality: Buys the round before anyone asks. Agrees with whoever spoke last, then repeats it at the next table as if they'd sworn to it. Goes still when the colony comes up, and stays still until whoever raised it has finished.
characters.speech: Slow and warm. Every sentence is a question he knows the answer to. Calls anyone younger than him cousin.

characters.name: Bastien Orlo
characters.description: The Pact's returns officer, who brings runaways back to their contracts and carries the Arbiters' copy of the runaway's indenture.
characters.appearance: Tall and clean-shaven, gloves on in all weather, an oilcloth satchel chained to his belt.
characters.personality: Waits as long as it takes. Follows the contract to the letter, and takes no money, no drink and no excuses. Keeps a tally of every runaway he has brought back, and reads it aloud to the next one.
characters.speech: Formal, exact and quiet. Quotes the contract clause by clause.

characters.personality: Lazy where nobody's watching and brisk where somebody is. Takes coin to look the other way.

characters.name: The Hushed traders
characters.description: Two of the Hushed, who come to the Woed's edge in the mornings to sell what the wood gives, tamecap included.
characters.appearance: Two figures in undyed wool, hoods up, never more than an arm's length apart.
characters.personality: Sell, and say nothing else to outsiders. Won't deal with fen folk at all.

relationships.shape: Cadfan carries Morwen's remedies to Caerwyn and takes a third. She is the one person in the fen he doesn't cheat.
relationships.together: She hands him jars through the hatch and counts them back.

wants.morwen: her goods sold and her name kept out of it

bands.label: They share a name and nothing else now.
Blood holds them together, and not much more.
They fight the way family fights, and close ranks against anyone else.
Each would take a blow meant for the other.
Each will take a loss if it costs the other more.
Every exchange is being scored. Courtesy, when it appears, is a move.
They measure themselves against each other, and both know the other is doing it.
Neither would say it aloud, but each has stopped hoping the other fails.
The contest is still running. It has stopped being the point of them.
Each is looking for the way out of the arrangement.
They work together and watch each other while they do.
They have stopped testing each other and started relying on it.
Neither could say when it stopped being an arrangement.
Each would cross the street to avoid the other.
They are wary of each other, and their manners say so.
They know each other's names and not much else.
Each has done the other a good turn, and both remember it.
Each would vouch for the other to someone who mattered.
They are glad to see each other and would not go out of their way for it.
The warmth is real and out of practice.
They tell each other things first.
Their plans assume each other. Neither has checked whether that was ever agreed.

actions.name: Work a shift at the smokehouse
actions.summary: A day's hauling peat and hanging eels, for a coin.
actions.input: I ask for a shift at the smokehouse.
actions.outcome: You take a shift hauling peat and hanging eels in the smoke, and come out coughing with a coin for it.

actions.name: Work a night on the long fence
actions.summary: On a run night, Ellis's crew needs hands. A coin for the night.
actions.input: I ask Ellis for a place on the fence tonight.
actions.outcome: Ellis puts you on the end of the fence with a lantern and a gaff, and pays you a coin at dawn for a night of hauling eels.

actions.name: Hire Gethin for the day
actions.summary: One coin buys Gethin and his flatboat until midnight.
actions.input: I hire Gethin and his flatboat for the day.
actions.outcome: Gethin takes your coin first, then asks where to.

actions.name: Buy Gethin's old flatboat
actions.summary: Ten coin for a flatboat of your own: the water routes open to you.
actions.input: I ask Gethin what he wants for his old flatboat.
actions.outcome: Gethin sells you his old flatboat and a pole for ten coin, and shows you where it leaks.

actions.name: Pay Bronwen for what she has heard
actions.summary: Two coin for what Corran talks about when he has been drinking.
actions.input: I put two coins on the bar and ask Bronwen what Corran talks about when he's been drinking.
actions.outcome: Bronwen pockets the coins and tells you Corran asks every crew where the patrol camps, and that he went out to Grey Water alone.

actions.name: Count the patrol for Corran
actions.summary: Corran pays ten coin to have the patrol at Grey Water counted.
actions.input: I tell Corran I'll go and count the patrol for him.
actions.outcome: Corran pays you ten coin to go out to Grey Water and count the patrol's men, and to be seen doing it.

actions.name: Tell Meyrick what Corran is doing
actions.summary: With something on Corran, take it to the bog-keeper before the patrol comes.
actions.input: I tell Meyrick what Corran has been doing out at Grey Water.
actions.outcome: Meyrick hears you out without a word, then takes it to Nest. By evening the fen knows Corran meant to bring the patrol down on Nest's island.

actions.name: Ask Nest to let Ellis go
actions.summary: Once Nest has given way to you, she can let Ellis go after the patrol.
actions.input: I tell Nest the patrol won't stop at me, and Ellis should go now.
actions.outcome: Nest looks at her grandson a long time, then nods once. Ellis is out of the door with his spear before she has finished.

actions.name: Take Morwen's errand
actions.summary: Morwen needs tamecap from the Woed's edge, and pays for it.
actions.input: I tell Morwen I'll go to the Woed's edge for her.
actions.outcome: Morwen pushes ten coin through the hatch and tells you what tamecap looks like, where the Hushed sell it, and that nobody in the fen will help you get there.

actions.name: Give Morwen the tamecap
actions.summary: Bring the cure while it can still work.
actions.outcome: Morwen takes the tamecap without a word and shuts the back door behind her. When she comes out her hands are shaking, and she says the girl is asleep, and means it.

actions.name: Have Morwen burn out the ink
actions.summary: Her price is paid. Lye and a hot knife take the Pact's ink off your arm.
actions.input: I hold out my arm and ask Morwen to take the ink off.
actions.outcome: Morwen straps your arm to the table, paints it with lye and takes the ink out with a hot knife. It takes an hour. The smell stays longer.

actions.name: Ask Cadfan about the drowned man
actions.summary: With something on Cadfan, ask what he keeps under the barrels at the back of the smokehouse.
actions.input: I tell Cadfan I know what he keeps under the barrels at the back of the smokehouse.
actions.outcome: Cadfan looks at the door, then lifts the barrels. Underneath, wrapped in sacking, is a drowned human about your size, a Low Road passenger he lost on the channel last month. He is yours, if you can get him burned.

actions.name: Burn the drowned man under your name
actions.summary: With Meyrick won over, the fen can burn the body as yours and tell the patrol.
actions.input: I ask Meyrick to burn the drowned man under my name and send word to the patrol.
actions.outcome: Meyrick lights the pyre himself and sends word to Grey Water that the colony's runaway drowned in the fen and has been burned. By morning the patrol has it in writing.

actions.name: Buy out the contract through Edric
actions.summary: A hundred coin to the Arbiters and ten for Edric. On paper, you are free.
actions.input: I ask Edric what it would cost to buy out a Port Covenant indenture.
actions.outcome: Edric counts your coin twice, takes his ten, and fills in a release from the Arbiters' agent in Caerwyn with your name. He seals it in front of you.

actions.name: Book a place on the Low Road
actions.summary: Twenty coin buys a barrel on the next boat to Caerwyn.
actions.input: I ask Cadfan what a place in one of his barrels costs.
actions.outcome: Cadfan takes twenty coin and shows you the barrel: air holes under the rim, eels packed on top. The boat leaves on Monday.

actions.name: Load Cadfan's barrels on boat day
actions.summary: Cadfan pays ten coin to load barrels onto Edric's boat without looking in them.
actions.input: I offer to load Cadfan's barrels.
actions.outcome: You load Cadfan's barrels onto Edric's boat while Cadfan talks prices. Two of them are heavier than eels. Cadfan pays you ten coin for not noticing.

goods.name: a moss dressing
goods.description: Dried sphagnum moss packed in a linen wrap, for soaking up blood and keeping a wound clean.

goods.name: a willow draught
goods.description: Willow bark steeped bitter in a stoppered jar, for fever and pain.

goods.name: a peat smoke pot
goods.description: A clay pot of smouldering peat that fills a room or a reed bed with smoke.

goods.name: a fen pole
goods.description: A long ash pole for vaulting ditches and testing mud. It helps on chases and crossings in the fen.

goods.name: an eel spear
goods.description: A barbed iron head on an ash shaft, made for eels and good for worse.

goods.name: a tamecap
goods.description: A small grey mushroom from the Woed, the only known cure for Rabitis in its early stages.

goods.name: a forged release
goods.description: A release from an indenture in a fair copy of the Arbiters' hand. It helps Flair with the patrol and its officer.

scenario.title: In the net at the long fence
scenario.opening:
*The net comes up out of the black water all at once, and you come up with it. Eels slide over your arms and down your collar, cold and thick and still fighting, and the cord bites into the backs of your knees. A lantern swings out on a pole and stops a hand from your face.*

*Three salamanders crouch on the plank walk along the top of the fence, black hides beaded with wet, orange blotches gone dull in the lantern light. The nearest has an eel spear across his knees. Its barbs are close enough to count.*

*The one holding the lantern leans closer.* That's no eel.

It's in our net. *The one with the spear leans out and turns your wrist over with the butt of it, so the light falls on the ink.* Colony.

*Far back across the fen, toward the causeway, a horn blows twice. All three of them look that way. Then they look back at you.*
